analysis.investment_thesis: Deepak Fertilisers is the closest of this cohort to Graham's standards — nine consecutive profitable years, reasonable interest coverage of 4.7x, and a forward P/E approaching the 15x threshold. However, at P/B of 2.38 and D/E of 0.62, the stock trades above the margin of safety a disciplined value investor demands.
key_strengths: Nine unbroken years of positive net earnings (2016–2025), satisfying the multi-year earnings track record requirement
Interest coverage of ~4.7x (EBIT INR 1,925 Cr ÷ finance cost INR 413 Cr), comfortably above the 3.5x floor
Operating cash flow positive all five recent years; OCF rebounded sharply to INR 1,880 Cr in FY25 after weakness in FY23-24
key_risks: P/B of 2.38 exceeds the 1.5x ceiling; Graham Number (√22.5 × EPS ~₹75 × BVPS ~₹515) approximates ₹931 vs. the current price of ₹1,230 — a ~32% premium to intrinsic book-based value
Debt/equity of 0.62 breaches the 0.5 limit; borrowings have expanded from INR 2,593 Cr (FY21) to INR 4,440 Cr (FY25) to fund heavy capex, with CWIP at INR 2,230 Cr
Earnings volatility is high — net profit swung from INR 73 Cr (FY19) to INR 1,221 Cr (FY23) and back to INR 468 Cr (FY24), making normalized earning power difficult to establish
red_flags: Fertiliser revenues are partly subsidy-dependent, introducing regulatory risk outside management's control
Free cash flow was negative in FY23 (−INR 716 Cr) and FY24 (−INR 94 Cr) due to the capex cycle — reported profits overstated true cash generation in those years
Finance costs growing at 13.7% CAGR (faster than net profit in early years), signalling rising debt service burden
analysis.detailed_analysis:
DEEPAKFERT passes the most Graham tests of any stock in this set: a long positive-earnings history, adequate interest coverage, and a P/E of 17.8x (only modestly above the 15x ceiling) with forward P/E of 13.4x suggesting improving near-term earnings. The net profit CAGR of 26.2% over nine years is impressive, though heavily distorted by the commodity supercycle in FY22–23 and a reversal in FY24. The company's chemical and nitric acid volumes serve genuine industrial demand, providing some earnings stability.

The disqualifying factors from a strict value standpoint are the P/B of 2.38 (paying INR 2.38 for each rupee of net assets), the debt load that has grown meaningfully, and the cyclicality of both fertiliser and petrochemical businesses. A patient investor might revisit if the price declined ~25–30% to approach the Graham Number of ~₹930. As it stands, there is no margin of safety — the stock is fairly priced at best, not cheap.
